original_test_intent: For each Always off, Always on and Previous BIOS AC Loss Control choice, verify the setting can be saved/re-read and that the SUT reaches the specified power state after one controlled G3 AC-loss/restore cycle.
original_method: In an approved isolated maintenance window, bind the SUT/BMC/PDU, capture baseline, have an operator set and re-read one BIOS choice, correlate the configured policy through protected OOB evidence, perform exactly one authorized full G3 AC cut/restore with state-specific preparation, observe the resulting state, then restore and verify the baseline before the next choice or release.
manual_activity: The owner approves target, mapping, initial state, physical AC path and each BIOS write/G3 cycle. A qualified operator sets/re-reads BIOS and controls or witnesses AC removal/restoration and resulting state.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC/board, BIOS and AC-feed/PDU identity
Owner-approved BIOS labels and OOB policy mapping
Baseline AC Loss Control value and restore plan
For each policy, required pre-G3 platform state and expected post-restore state
Qualified BIOS operator and protected console
Approved physical or managed AC cut/restore path with dwell time
Workload isolation, power sequencing, reconnect timeouts and recovery runbook
Protected credentials, redaction and evidence policy
safety_requirements: Quarantine all AFULnx/afuefix64.efi/image/flash-loop instructions from the duplicate variant
Obtain explicit approval before every BIOS write, reboot and G3 cycle
Verify SUT, BMC and exact AC-feed/PDU outlet before power action
Ensure no workload, firmware write, storage flush or other test is active
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Never expose default or command-line credentials
Run exactly one approved cycle per policy with no automatic retry
Stop on save/readback mismatch, wrong outlet, unexpected state, timeout or recovery failure
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only identity, baseline, workload and power-path checks
Coordinate operator BIOS set/save/re-entry for exactly one policy
Collect configured-policy/OOB correlation without treating event history as policy
After separate explicit approval, invoke or witness one bounded AC cut/restore through the verified path
Observe off/on/previous result using BMC and host evidence
Stop on any anomaly and assist only the approved recovery
Restore and verify baseline under approval
engineer_actions: Approve the three-policy order, expected states, dwell time and each mutation/cycle
Validate AC-feed topology and Previous-state setup
Supervise BIOS and physical power actions
Own recovery decisions and final PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The always-off IPMI step is partial and cannot replace BIOS save/re-read or physical G3 observation. Its AMI flash package, flash logs and bricking warning are wrong-variant contamination and prohibited.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved operator BIOS path plus protected configured-policy readback; only after a separate per-policy confirmation, perform one controlled G3 AC cut/restore on the verified feed and record actual state. Never flash BIOS in this case.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All three named policies, save/re-read, chassis status correlation, functional cycle and 40/40-minute estimates remain; fixed credentials and log clearing are rejected.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For each policy maintain a transaction record containing initial state, BIOS before/set/save/re-read, configured-policy correlation, verified feed, AC-off/on timestamps and dwell, observed result, health checks and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact target/feed binding, state-specific Previous setup, one-cycle limit, safe stop/recovery and duplicate-variant quarantine.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Policy display/readback alone cannot prove post-G3 behavior, and one always-off cycle cannot cover always-on or previous-state restoration.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong feed or failed recovery can interrupt other equipment or strand the SUT; Previous behavior is meaningless unless the pre-loss state is explicitly controlled.

project_override_considerations: A managed PDU/Rack Manager may automate the physical cycle only when the exact outlet topology and recovery path are approved. No project override may borrow the same-code Type 45 or repeated-flash workflow, and all three source policies remain independently evidenced.
expected_evidence: Variant identity and explicit quarantine of rows 690/1539 methods
Redacted SUT/BMC/BIOS/PDU identity, approvals, baseline and expected policy/state matrix
Per policy: BIOS before/set/save/re-entry evidence and protected configured-policy correlation
Per policy: pre-G3 state, verified outlet, AC-off/on timeline/dwell and observed resulting state
Boot/BMC/host reachability, preserved SEL/OS/firmware events and anomaly record
Baseline restoration/readback and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master Items, Procedure and Criteria coherently require AC Loss Control persistence and functional cycling for three policies. The BIOS-flash package/log/risk contamination is confined to the prior AI columns caused by duplicate code and is explicitly quarantined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The hybrid test is identifiable once the owner supplies the operator, exact AC path, policy mapping, state setup, approvals and recovery plan.

review_improvement: Prevents duplicate-code flash contamination, requires separate save/readback and actual G3 evidence for all three policies, and makes Previous-state setup plus feed recovery auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: AC Loss Control has two independent claims: firmware retained the selected policy, and hardware behavior after a true G3 transition matched it. The latter requires verified loss of AC—not a reboot or chassis-status string—and Previous additionally requires a known pre-loss power state, so each policy needs its own bounded transaction.
